AgentMode.description: How a run's work is divided between models (owner decisions M1-M4).
AgentMode.title: AgentMode

AgentModeConfig.description:
Which models play which roles in one run.

- ``single``: ``lead_model`` is the one model. No workers, no panel.
- ``tiered``: ``lead_model`` plans, reviews and takes over failing steps;
  ``worker_models`` (1 to 4) implement steps.
- ``crowd``: as ``tiered``, plus ``panel_models`` (2 to 5) whose plans the
  lead merges.
AgentModeConfig.title: AgentModeConfig

AgentModeDefault.description:
The agent mode a new run uses unless it names its own (doc 19b).

``saved`` is false when the owner has not saved a default yet, so the
config shown is the one derived from settings (two tiered, today's models).
AgentModeDefault.title: AgentModeDefault

AgentRole.description: Who an agent is in the hierarchy: the lead plans and reviews, juniors implement.
AgentRole.title: AgentRole

AgentStatus.description: Whether an agent row is usable and busy.
AgentStatus.title: AgentStatus

ApprovalKind.description:
What a human is being asked to approve (doc 03 task 3).

``plan``, ``escalation``, ``budget``, ``pr_open`` and ``merge`` are graph
interrupts; ``command`` is asked *inside* an agent turn by the runtime's
permission hook (2026-11-12 review, section 3.1).
ApprovalKind.title: ApprovalKind

ApprovalPage.description:
The approval inbox list, plus the workspace's pending count.

``total_pending`` ignores the list filters on purpose: the nav badge needs
one call that still shows the real count when the page is filtered.
ApprovalPage.title: ApprovalPage

ApprovalRead.description: An approval request and, once decided, its outcome.
ApprovalRead.title: ApprovalRead

ApprovalStatus.description: The outcome of an approval request; ``expired`` is the default-deny timeout.
ApprovalStatus.title: ApprovalStatus

ApprovalWaitSummary.description: Human wait time for approvals over a window (doc 18b).
ApprovalWaitSummary.title: ApprovalWaitSummary

AutoModeStatus.description:
Which model families run in auto mode.

In auto mode a command the policy would ask about runs without waiting for
a human; denied commands, the sandbox and protected-file writes are unchanged.
AutoModeStatus.title: AutoModeStatus

AutoModeUpdate.description: Switch auto mode on or off per family. An omitted family is left as it is.
AutoModeUpdate.title: AutoModeUpdate

CatalogModelRead.description: One model Gaia can put in a role, with its list prices (USD per 1M tokens).
CatalogModelRead.title: CatalogModelRead

CiStatus.description: The part of a GitHub checks rollup Gaia cares about (doc 15).
CiStatus.title: CiStatus

CommandSuggestion.description: A command prefix suggested from the owner's past approvals in one repository.
CommandSuggestion.title: CommandSuggestion

CommandSuggestionList.description: Suggested allowed commands, most often approved first.
CommandSuggestionList.title: CommandSuggestionList

CostByDay.description: LLM spend for one UTC day over a window (doc 18b).
CostByDay.title: CostByDay

CostByModel.description: LLM spend for one provider/model pair over a window (doc 18b).
CostByModel.title: CostByModel

DecideAccepted.description: The 202 acknowledgement for a graph-gate decision.
DecideAccepted.title: DecideAccepted

DecideRequest.description:
A human decision on one approval (doc 14).

``remember`` is valid only when approving a command: the command's prefix
(``payload.remember_prefix``) is added to the repository's allowed commands
as well.
DecideRequest.title: DecideRequest

EventHistory.description: One page of a run's event history.
EventHistory.title: EventHistory

EventRecord.description:
The wire format of one event, and what the bus hands subscribers.

Persisted events always have an integer ``seq`` and an ``id``. A
``stream.gap`` marker is transport-only: it has ``seq=None`` and ``id=None``
and is never written to the database.
EventRecord.title: EventRecord

EventType.description:
Every event the bus can carry (doc 13).

``stream.gap`` is transport-only: the bus inserts it into a subscriber's
queue when that subscriber overflowed, but it is never written to the
``event`` table.
EventType.title: EventType

LLMProvider.description:
A model provider Gaia can reach through its LLM gateway (doc 07b, 19a).

The value is the gateway route segment (``/llm/<provider>/...``), the
``provider`` stored on a run token and on ``llm_usage`` rows, and the
``provider`` key of a model in ``prices.toml``.
LLMProvider.title: LLMProvider

ModelCatalog.description: Every provider and every priced model (``GET /models``).
ModelCatalog.title: ModelCatalog

ModelTier.description:
A model's rough capability class, used to suggest models for a role (19a).

It is guidance shown in the UI, never a rule: the owner may put any model
in any role.
ModelTier.title: ModelTier

PauseAllRequest.description: Reason for pausing every run. Global, not per workspace: Gaia is single-user.
PauseAllRequest.title: PauseAllRequest

PauseAllResult.description: The ids paused by this call (usually empty when already paused).
PauseAllResult.title: PauseAllResult

PauseStatus.description: Whether the global kill switch is on (doc 18a).
PauseStatus.title: PauseStatus

ProviderCost.description: Today's spend for one LLM provider.
ProviderCost.title: ProviderCost

ProviderStatus.description: One LLM provider and whether its API key is in the keychain (19a).
ProviderStatus.title: ProviderStatus

PullRequestRead.description: A PR as the pull-request list route shows it (doc 15b).
PullRequestRead.title: PullRequestRead

PullRequestState.description: The part of a GitHub PR's state Gaia cares about (doc 15).
PullRequestState.title: PullRequestState

RepositoryCreate.description:
Register a repository.

``name`` is optional: the route defaults it to the repository root's
directory name. The commands are argv lists (never a shell string), and they
are the owner's registration-time values, never read from the repository.
RepositoryCreate.title: RepositoryCreate

RepositoryDetailRead.description: A repository with the two counts the dashboard shows.
RepositoryDetailRead.title: RepositoryDetailRead

RepositoryUpdate.description:
Change a registered repository's commands.

Only the fields that are sent change; ``null`` clears a command. The path,
name and remote are not editable: they identify the repository.
``allowed_commands`` replaces the whole list; each entry is an argv prefix
an agent may run without asking.
RepositoryUpdate.title: RepositoryUpdate

ResumeAllResult.description: The ids that were ``paused`` and are now being relaunched.
ResumeAllResult.title: ResumeAllResult

RunCreate.description:
Start a run. The status starts at ``pending`` and cannot be set here.

``agent_config`` overrides the saved default for this run (doc 19b, M3).
``junior_runtime`` is the older per-run override, kept for API clients; it
cannot be combined with ``agent_config``.
RunCreate.title: RunCreate

RunCurrentStep.description: The first not-yet-completed step of a run, for the dashboard list.
RunCurrentStep.title: RunCurrentStep

RunDetail.description: Everything the run detail endpoint shows (doc 14).
RunDetail.title: RunDetail

RunPage.description: One page of runs and the cursor for the next page.
RunPage.title: RunPage

RunPullRequestRead.description: The PR fields a run detail shows, without the list route's repo context.
RunPullRequestRead.title: RunPullRequestRead

RunRead.description: A run, including the money that has been spent on it so far.
RunRead.title: RunRead

RunStatus.description:
Where a run is in the graph of ARCHITECTURE section 4.

``awaiting_approval`` covers every human gate between agent turns, and
``paused_budget`` the budget interrupt. ``failed`` and ``completed`` are
terminal; a failed run is resumed from its checkpoint instead of being
revived by a status change.
RunStatus.title: RunStatus

RunStepRead.description: One step of a run's plan.
RunStepRead.title: RunStepRead

RunStepStatus.description: Where a single step of the plan is (``run_step.status``).
RunStepStatus.title: RunStepStatus

RunSummary.description: One row of the dashboard runs list (doc 14).
RunSummary.title: RunSummary

RunTicketSummary.description: The ticket fields a run detail shows beside the run.
RunTicketSummary.title: RunTicketSummary

RunWorktreeSummary.description: The worktree fields a run detail shows.
RunWorktreeSummary.title: RunWorktreeSummary

RuntimeKind.description:
The harness behind an agent; ADR-001 (doc 08) picks which ones ship.

``native_claude`` and ``native_deepseek`` are the raw-API runtimes,
``claude_agent_sdk`` and ``cline_cli`` the harnesses. The values are stored
on ``agent.runtime`` and ``run.junior_runtime``, so they must not change
after the first migration without one.
RuntimeKind.title: RuntimeKind

SessionRead.description: The authenticated caller plus process-wide flags the UI needs (18b-2).
SessionRead.title: SessionRead

StreamTicket.description: The short-lived credential the UI puts in the SSE query string.
StreamTicket.title: StreamTicket

TicketCreate.description: Open a ticket. ``status`` is deliberately absent (see the module docstring).
TicketCreate.title: TicketCreate

TicketPage.description: One page of tickets and the cursor for the next one.
TicketPage.title: TicketPage

TicketPatch.description: Update a ticket. ``status`` goes through the transition machine.
TicketPatch.title: TicketPatch

TicketRead.description: A ticket, with its status validated against :class:`TicketStatus`.
TicketRead.title: TicketRead

TicketStatus.description: Where a ticket is in the queue (doc 03 task 3).
TicketStatus.title: TicketStatus

TodayCosts.description: The numbers for the top bar's daily spend meter (doc 16).
TodayCosts.title: TodayCosts

WorktreeItemRead.title: WorktreeItemRead

WorktreeListRead.description: The worktree list: rows plus paths git knows that no row claims.
WorktreeListRead.title: WorktreeListRead

WorktreeStatus.description: Lifecycle of a git worktree (doc 05 owns the transitions).
WorktreeStatus.title: WorktreeStatus

info.summary: Local-first control plane for a hierarchy of AI coding agents.
info.title: Gaia

get.description:
Answer without touching the database or the keychain.

A probe that failed because the database was busy, or the keychain was
locked, would report the wrong problem. "The process answers HTTP" is what
this says, and it is the only thing a supervisor needs.
Return the mode and models a new run uses unless it names its own (doc 19b).

put.description:
Save the default for new runs. Runs already started keep their own config.

Every model must be in the catalog. Provider keys are checked when a run
starts, not here, so a default can name a provider before its key is added.

get.description: Return which model families run commands without asking.

patch.description:
Switch auto mode on or off for one or both families.

It takes effect on each agent's next command that would need approval; a
command already waiting for approval still waits.

get.description: Return whether the orchestrator is paused, and since when.

post.description:
Cancel every live graph task and pause every queued run.

Idempotent: pausing again returns the runs it paused this time, which is
usually an empty list.
Clear the global flag and relaunch every run it paused.

get.description: Return the workspace's agents, newest first by UUIDv7 id.

schema.title: Response List Agents Api V1 Agents Get

get.description:
Return approvals, oldest first by default, optionally filtered.

``decided=true`` with ``order=newest`` is the inbox's "recent decisions"
view (lead review of 17d: oldest-first made it show the oldest 50).

``total_pending`` always counts the workspace's pending approvals, whatever
filters the caller passed: the badge makes one call and must not change with
the page. ``ApprovalRepo`` keeps every read inside the authenticated
workspace.

parameters.description: Only approvals that are no longer pending.
parameters.name: decided

schema.description: Only approvals that are no longer pending.
schema.title: Decided

post.description:
Record a human decision and, for graph gates, resume the run.

Command approvals are answered inside the runtime's turn and do not resume
the graph (doc 14). Graph-gate decisions are applied asynchronously by the
resumed node, so this route returns 202 and never marks the row decided
itself.

get.description: Return the UTC day's spend, budget and per-provider breakdown.
Return the caller the bearer token resolved to, plus process flags.

Return runs, spend and approval wait metrics for the last UTC days.

The window covers ``days`` UTC calendar days ending today (UTC), which keeps
"last 1 day" aligned to midnight UTC rather than a rolling 24 hours.

Return every provider with whether its key is set, and every priced model.

A model is ``available`` when its provider's key is in the keychain (or in
demo mode). Key values are never read into the response.
get.summary: List the models Gaia can use

get.description: Return the workspace's PRs, newest first, optionally filtered by state.
Return every repository registered in this workspace.

schema.title: Response List Repositories Api V1 Repositories Get

post.description: Validate ``local_path``, detect its origin and default branch, and add a row.

delete.description:
Delete the row only. No file or directory on disk is touched.

Refused with 409 while the repository has tickets or live worktrees: the
foreign keys cascade, so deleting the row would silently delete every
ticket, run, approval and usage record that hangs off it (lead review of 06).

get.description: Return the repository plus its worktree count and active run count.

patch.description:
Set or clear the setup, test and allowed commands; only the fields sent change.

The commands are owner-registered values (never read from the repository),
so editing them is an owner action and is audited. A run that is already
past setup keeps what it started with; the next run uses the new values.
patch.summary: Change a repository's setup, test or allowed commands

get.description:
Prefixes of commands you approved in this repository that still ask.

Read-only: nothing is added until the owner saves them as allowed commands.
get.summary: Suggest allowed commands from past approvals

get.description: Return the workspace's runs, newest first.

post.description: Start the graph for ``ticket_id`` and return the new run row.

get.description: Return one run with its steps, worktree, approvals and PR.

post.description: Cancel a live run, keep its worktree, and mark the run cancelled.

get.description:
Return the committed plus uncommitted diff, capped at ``max_bytes``.

Git runs after the database rows are loaded and the session is closed: a GET
must not change git state, and no git call may sit inside a DB transaction.

Return events after ``after`` for one run, oldest first.

The run is loaded through ``ScopedRepo``, so a run in another workspace is
exactly the same 404 as a missing one.

Stream events with ``text/event-stream``.

A missing, used or expired ticket is the same 401 envelope; the route never
distinguishes them to a client. The ``Last-Event-ID`` header wins over the
``last_event_id`` query parameter (see the module docstring for why both
exist).

post.description: Exchange the bearer token for a short-lived SSE ticket.

get.description: Return one page of tickets, filtered by status, repository and title.

post.description: Create a ticket in ``repo_id`` after proving the repo is in this workspace.

get.description: Return one ticket, or 404 - the same answer for another workspace.

patch.description: Update text fields and apply a legal status transition, if one is given.

get.description: Return a repository's worktrees with orphan and dirty flags.

delete.description:
Remove a worktree from disk and mark its row ``removed``.

The row is kept as history. A dirty worktree is refused unless ``force`` is
set; a tampered worktree is always refused.
